name: Ramipril
route_note: oral capsule or tablet once or twice daily

discovery.note: A long-acting prodrug ACE inhibitor with high tissue-ACE affinity. Year of the first patent, per Wikipedia (patented 1981, approved for medical use 1989).

tagline: ACE inhibitor whose HOPE trial showed protection in high-risk vascular patients
summary: Ramipril is a prodrug ACE inhibitor hydrolysed to ramiprilat. Beyond hypertension and heart failure after myocardial infarction, the HOPE trial showed it reduces heart attack, stroke and cardiovascular death in high-risk patients without heart failure.
mechanism: Hepatic esterases convert ramipril to ramiprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, lowering angiotensin II and aldosterone and increasing bradykinin.
The result is vasodilation, natriuresis and reduced glomerular pressure; its slow dissociation from ACE gives a long terminal half-life and once-daily dosing.
uses: Reduction of risk of MI, stroke and cardiovascular death in high-risk patients aged ≥55
Diabetic and non-diabetic nephropathy (in some markets)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Altace.

history.title: AIRE
history.detail: Ramipril reduces mortality in patients with clinical heart failure after acute MI.

history.title: HOPE
history.detail: Ramipril reduces cardiovascular death, MI and stroke in high-risk patients without heart failure.

history.title: ONTARGET
history.detail: Telmisartan is non-inferior to ramipril, and combining the two adds harm without benefit.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic ramipril becomes available in the US.

safety.boxed_warning: Fetal toxicity: drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus; discontinue when pregnancy is detected.

facts: The HOPE trial was a major influence on the use of ACE inhibitors for vascular protection independent of blood pressure.

references.title: HOPE Study Investigators. Effects of an angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor, ramipril, on cardiovascular events in high-risk patients. N Engl J Med 2000
